newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar ends around highs, trade light.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar ends around highs, trade light.

text.p: White sugar futures inched back up to the day's highs and closed steadier on Wednesday, although conditions remained slow in the evening session.
Traders said the market needs fresh physical offtake to snap out of its lethargy, and most attention was focussed on the white premium and the raws market after its recent rally.
March closed at $304.20 a tonne, up $2.60, while May finished at the same level to post a $2.40 gain. LIFFE turnover was a light 749 lots.
In physicals, the EU awarded 45,400 tonnes of current series white sugar with export rebates of a maximum 47.002 European Currency Units (Ecus) per 100 kilos at its weekly tender.

Poland's Agriculture Ministry said it wanted to raise the quota for domestic sugar sales by 130,000 tonnes to 1.63 million tonnes for the 1996/1997 growing season to help absorb this year's sugar surplus.
